clue.text: Something that's essential when bringing back fruit

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the way it came, so the two pieces are read right to left

parts.note: something essential is 'a must'
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A shopper insists on one essential item whenever they bring home fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing back' turns A MUST plus AS, giving the whole run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A small loose-skinned citrus orange is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Joint holders

parts.note: reads like partners who share ownership, but means pins that keep a roasting joint of meat together

explanation.surface: Two people who jointly own something.
explanation.walkthrough: A joint is also a cut of meat for roasting, held by long metal pins.
explanation.definitionFit: Long pins pushed through meat hold it for cooking.

clue.text: He may be prepared to sell his land

definitions.text: He may be prepared to sell his land

parts.words: He may be prepared to sell his land
parts.note: reads as a farmer selling property, but 'sell' means betray: someone ready to sell out his country

explanation.surface: A landowner thinking of putting his farm on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: To sell one's country is to betray it to an enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrayer of his country is willing to hand his homeland over to the enemy.

clue.text: Thrown out of bed earlier than arranged

indicators.note: places the first piece ahead of the second in this down answer

parts.note: someone out of bed is up
something arranged is set, like a set time

explanation.surface: Someone tossed out of bed before their alarm was due.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrown, like a rider or a person shocked, is knocked off balance or overturned.

clue.text: Gives up an office from a basic date

indicators.note: the answer is made from these letters, so they are rearranged rather than read as they stand

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a job on a dull, ordinary day.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' before the fodder is only a link word, and 'from' is a soft anagram signal meaning made out of.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who renounces the throne resigns from a high post.

clue.text: Way of selling established in ancient times

definitions.meaning: ... selling is a sales scheme where recruits sell to further recruits
the great Egyptian tombs were built thousands of years ago

explanation.surface: A sales method that has been around since antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a tiered sales scheme and the huge Egyptian tombs share this name.

clue.text: Translation of prose is a problem

indicators.note: a translation changes a text's form, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student finds rendering prose into another language difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzling question or tricky problem is a teaser.

clue.text: Yard chase forged and immediately available money

indicators.note: forged things are fakes made up anew, so the letters of both words are reworked

explanation.surface: A chase across a yard and some counterfeit cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Money on hand to spend at once is spending money held in notes and coins.

clue.text: Complaint that bad French is sung?

parts.note: mal is French for bad
an aria is a song sung solo in an opera

explanation.surface: A grumble that someone sings in poor French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' and 'is' are link words; complaint here means an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be an ailment, and this is a mosquito-borne fever.

clue.text: Security is lifted in the store

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a depot is a store or warehouse

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifting a word turns it upwards so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: A guarded item has been stolen from the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'lifted' means read upwards, which reverses the short word before it goes inside the store.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid as a guarantee, such as on a rental, is a security.

clue.text: Slipped away, unusually pleased

indicators.note: something done unusually is out of its normal order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone left quietly, oddly happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has slipped away has passed by.

clue.text: Calls round with work of ornamental edging

indicators.note: turned round, the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone visits with a piece of decorative trimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calls round' looks like visiting, but 'round' is the anagram signal; 'with' and 'of' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A border of curved half-circles copies the outline of a shell and trims fabric.

clue.text: Property conveyance?

parts.note: an estate is landed property
a car is a means of conveyance

explanation.surface: A legal transfer of property, as a solicitor would handle.
explanation.walkthrough: Conveyance is also the legal term for transferring property, which is the false lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A long car with a rear door and big load space is also a vehicle named after property.

clue.text: Measures the' mast beams

definitions.meaning: units of length of three feet
spars hung across a ship's mast to carry sails

explanation.surface: Someone sizes up the beams of a ship's mast.
explanation.definitionFit: Both units of three feet and sail spars on a mast share this name.

clue.text: When indisposed, one gets out of these classes

definitions.text: When indisposed, one gets out of these
definitions.meaning: a person feeling unwell is said to be out of them

explanation.surface: A sick person stays away from lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinds or types of thing, and the idiom 'out of' them for being unwell.

clue.text: Give up on French return

parts.note: sur is French for on
to render is to give back or return

explanation.surface: Someone yields after a trip back to France.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield to an enemy is to hand oneself over.

clue.text: Act as a dismantler?

parts.note: reads like playing a role on stage, but means doing the job of someone who takes things to pieces

explanation.surface: An actor cast as a demolition worker.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase could also mean taking on a role, a stage sense of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle is to separate something into its pieces.

clue.text: He has taking ways with children

definitions.text: He has taking ways with children

parts.words: He has taking ways with children
parts.note: taking ways usually means charm, but here means literally snatching children away

explanation.surface: A man who is charming and good with youngsters.
explanation.definitionFit: An abductor seizes children, often for ransom.

clue.text: One thing one doesn't expect to be

definitions.text: One thing one doesn't expect to be

parts.words: One thing one doesn't expect to be
parts.note: by definition one cannot anticipate being caught off guard

explanation.surface: A riddle about a state nobody anticipates.
explanation.definitionFit: Being astonished means meeting the unexpected.

clue.text: Favourable weather forecast but fear it's incorrect

indicators.note: the letters are wrongly ordered and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: The forecast is good, but someone worries it is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link word; the barometer marking for settled weather is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The marking on a barometer for settled sunny weather.

clue.text: Stand for the speaker

parts.note: could be standing in for a speaker, but means a raised platform

explanation.surface: Someone substitutes for the person giving a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform from which someone addresses an audience.

clue.text: Signed the driver to stop-it's a hold up

definitions.meaning: thumbing a lift from a passing motorist

explanation.surface: A hitch-hiker flags down a car, causing a delay.
explanation.definitionFit: Thumbing a lift, and a snag that delays things.

clue.text: Impressive work by the bookmaker

parts.note: a bookmaker usually takes bets, but here binds books and impresses designs on the covers

explanation.surface: A betting shop doing remarkable business.
explanation.walkthrough: Impressive means pressed in: decoration stamped into leather bindings.
explanation.definitionFit: Decoration stamped or pressed into a leather book cover.

clue.text: Fit to work like a horse

definitions.text: Fit to work like a horse

parts.words: Fit to work like a horse
parts.note: sounds like being strong enough for hard labour, but means equipping an animal for draught work

explanation.surface: Someone healthy enough to toil very hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To put straps and tack on an animal so it can pull a load.

clue.text: Set a test, an oral test

indicators.note: set means arranged or placed anew, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An examiner sets a paper, including a spoken exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Sampling food in the mouth tests its flavour.

clue.text: Where players have "their exits and their entrances"?

definitions.text: Where players have "their exits and their entrances"?

parts.words: Where players have "their exits and their entrances"?
parts.note: quotes Shakespeare's 'All the world's a stage', taken literally for actors' comings and goings at a theatre

explanation.surface: A line from As You Like It about life as a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors arrive and leave a theatre by this back entrance.

clue.text: Kid had a swing, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word is said aloud and the spelling changed

parts.note: to have a swing is to have swayed

explanation.surface: A child played on a swing.
explanation.walkthrough: Kid is both a child and soft goatskin leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid leather and napped leather are both soft fine leathers.

clue.text: Strange sense of locality in Germany

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd, so the letters are oddly reordered

explanation.surface: An odd feeling about a place in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: An industrial city in the Ruhr region of western Germany.

clue.text: A game to cut short

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A match that ends early.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten a book or text by trimming it.

clue.text: A leisure activity in father's day

parts.note: pa is father, and pa's is father's
time can mean a day or era, as in 'in my day'

explanation.surface: A hobby enjoyed on Father's Day.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobby is something done to fill spare hours enjoyably.

clue.text: Pity the sappers adopted signaller's system

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's sappers
Morse code is a system of dots and dashes used by signallers

explanation.surface: Army engineers took up a signalling code.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep regret or contrition, as in 'pity' meaning sorrow.

clue.text: Pulls out Greene's novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A Graham Greene book is withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive S here is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back on a promise or deal is to back out.
